sentences.text: The present Review Petition has been filed by the DDA seeking review of judgment dated 04.12.2017, wherein the captioned writ petition has been allowed.

The petitioner in the Writ Petition had filed the aforesaid writ petition seeking a declaration that the acquisition proceedings in respect of petitioner's land comprising in Khasra No. 47(15-5), 48(01-00) & 49(12- 19) total area 29 Bighas & 04 biswas having 1/12 th share measuring 02 Bigha and 09 Biswas situated in the Revenue Estate of Village Ghonda Gujaran Khadar, Shahdara, Delhi is deem to have been lapsed in view of Section 24(2) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement 2013 Act.
4.

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner was that the physical possession of the land has not been taken but during the course of hearing, it was represented that the petitioner would only claim compensation.

This Court in paragraph 8 noted the stand of the LAC in following manner:
"8. That although the Award in Question was made in the year 1992-93, yet no compensation has been offered, tendered or paid to the land owner/petitioner.

Under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, the acquisition proceedings initiated under the old Land Acquisition Act of 1894, by legal fiction, are deemed to have lapsed as the award was made 5 years or more prior to the commencement of 2013 Act, but no compensation has been offered, tendered or paid to the petitioner/
interested person.

5. It is a case where notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued on 23.06.1989; notification under Section 6 was issued on 20.06.1990 and an award was made on 19.06.1992.

6. The objection on behalf of the LAC was on the maintainability of the Writ Petition as the possession has been taken and the petitioner would not be entitled to the declaration on the strength of Section 24(2) of the Act.
7. This Court decided the Writ Petition by referring to the judgment of the Supreme Court in Pune Municipal Corp & Anr. Vs. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki & Ors (2014) 3 SCC 183.

It is also urged, that the Petitioner is not the owner of the land but the Gaon Sabha.
If that be so in view of the Judgement of the Constitution Bench in Indore Development Authority (Supra), the review petition is accepted.
